chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man nurses from the milk of a woman, everything from her offspring becomes forbidden to him, even if the child is from a man other than the one who nursed him with his milk. And when he nurses from the milk of a man, everything from that man's offspring becomes forbidden to him, even if it is from a woman other than the one who nursed him.
ai.seo_question: How does milk kinship affect marriage prohibitions when the biological parents differ from the nursing parents?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the mechanism of milk kinship (radāʿ) by establishing that the prohibition extends to the entire lineage of the nursing parent, irrespective of biological paternity or maternity. This principle is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining mahram relationships, ensuring that social and marital boundaries are preserved through the act of nursing rather than solely through bloodline. It underscores the juristic view that the milk of a parent creates a kinship bond equivalent to that of biological offspring.
